item.title: Izumo Soba: Dark Buckwheat Noodles in Stacked Bowls — Guide
item.description: Izumo soba is counted among the three great soba traditions of Japan, and it is distinctive from the first glance: because the whole buckwheat grain, husk included, is milled, the noodles are darker in colour, firmer, and much nuttier and more strongly flavoured than the pale soba of Tokyo. It is served in two classic styles. Warigo soba comes in a stack of three small round lacquer bowls, over which you pour the concentrated broth and condiments bowl by bowl.

item.title: Yamagata Soba: Hand-Cut Mountain Buckwheat — Guide
item.description: Yamagata is one of Tohoku’s great soba prefectures — the mountain climate and volcanic soil produce buckwheat of exceptional flavour, and the hand-cut soba tradition here emphasises a coarser, nuttier texture than Tokyo-style fine noodles. Cold zaru soba with local wasabi and a concentrated dashi tsuyu is the summer standard; autumn brings warm tororo soba with mountain yam. 🗓️ At a Glance Location Yamagata City & prefecture-wide Hours Restaurant hours Admission ~¥800–1,300 a bowl Time needed About 45 min Best time Summer (cold); autumn (tororo) What to Try Hand-cut soba with a coarser, nuttier texture.
